qti-content-body.p: Root — archa-: ancient, old (from Greek arkhaios 'ancient, old-fashioned,' itself built on arkhē, 'beginning, origin')
Suffix — -ic: characteristic of, having the quality of

Put it together: Archa- (ancient, old — Greek arkhaios, built on arkhē, 'beginning') + -ic (characteristic of) builds the meaning literally: having the character of ancient times — so old-fashioned it seems to belong to an earlier era. Note the spelling: the Greek root keeps its 'ch,' but it is pronounced like 'k' (ar-KAY-ik).
Use the root in a new word: archetype: Architecture students traveled to Chicago to sketch the building regarded as the archetype of the modern skyscraper.

qti-choice-interaction.qti-prompt: The words "archaic" and "archetype" share the Greek root 'arch-.' Considering that, what does "archetype" most nearly mean?
qti-choice-interaction.qti-simple-choice: the study of ancient life through objects people left behind
the first model of something, which later versions follow
a stored collection of old records and documents
an old-fashioned word or phrase surviving from an earlier age

qti-content-body.p: Studying ancient life through leftover objects is archaeology - arkhaios plus -logy, 'study of.' An archetype is not a field of study; its -type ending points at a pattern, not a science.
A stored collection of old records is an archive - from arkheion, the record office where a city's past was kept. An archetype is a single thing, not a roomful of documents.
An old-fashioned expression still lingering in the language is an archaism - the closest cousin to archaic itself. An archetype is not a leftover from the past; its -type half does different work.

Right - arch- carries the Greek arkhe, 'beginning, origin,' and an archetype is the beginning-stamp: arkhe plus typos, 'stamp, model,' the first pattern that everything after it follows. Archaic looks back at the same starting point - so old it belongs to the beginnings.

Not quite. All four options reach back to the Greek arkh- family, so age alone cannot settle it. The second half of archetype is -type, a stamp or pattern - ask what kind of thing a stamp is to everything printed from it.
